documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
KIF13B expression is lower in advanced human arterial and carotid lesions and in progressing mouse plaques.
Human findings are associative, not evidence that manipulating KIF13B changes human atherosclerosis.
GSE40231
40 non-atherosclerotic and 40 atherosclerotic arterial-wall samples showed lower KIF13B in atherosclerotic tissue.
Human carotid tissue
Early n=6 and advanced n=6 lesions showed lower KIF13B protein in advanced plaques, with macrophage co-localization.
Mouse progression
Ldlr-deficient mice, n=6 per group, showed lower plaque KIF13B after 20 versus 12 weeks of Western diet.
Results: The expression of KIF13B is negatively correlated with the progression of atherosclerosis in patients and mice; Figure 1 and Supplementary Figure S1.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
Global Kif13b loss worsened experimental atherosclerosis in Ldlr-deficient mice, but circulating lipids also increased in that model.
The global Ldlr-deficient comparison does not isolate a lipid-independent mechanism; Apoe-background observations did not show the same lipid effect.
Ldlr model
After 12 weeks of Western diet, control versus global Kif13b-deficient Ldlr-deficient mice had n=6 mice per group; lesions and circulating total cholesterol and triglycerides increased with Kif13b loss.
Plaque phenotype
Necrotic-core area rose up to approximately twofold, CD68-positive macrophage infiltration more than threefold, and apoptotic-cell accumulation increased.
Apoe background
Worsened plaques were also reported in the Apoe-deficient background without the same circulating-lipid change.
Results: Deletion of Kif13b in Ldlr−/− mice exacerbates atherosclerosis; Figure 2 and Supplementary Figure S2.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
Single-cell and macrophage analyses implicated altered macrophage states with lower Kif13b during experimental atherosclerosis.
The study-generated aortic single-cell comparison pooled five mice into one library per genotype; Results and Figure 3E disagree on diet duration, so no single definitive duration is assigned.
GSE155513
Figure 3 uses one single-cell library at each 8-week and 26-week high-fat-diet time point; macrophage abundance rose and Kif13b reduction was prominent in macrophages.
Study-generated single-cell
Five aortas were pooled per genotype into one library, yielding 14 clusters and eight cell types; Cd80-positive, Il1b-positive, Spp1-positive and Cd206-positive macrophage states were emphasized, with Kif13b loss associated with fewer Cd206-positive and more Il1b-positive and Spp1-positive states.
Independent observations
GSE215103 Apoe-deficient macrophage reanalysis and ox-LDL-treated BMDM and THP-1 experiments also showed lower KIF13B.
Results: Kif13b deficiency primarily affects macrophage dynamics in mouse atherosclerosis; Figure 3.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
Myeloid conditional deletion and Kif13b-deficient bone-marrow transfer worsened plaque phenotypes without corresponding plasma-lipid changes in their mouse models.
These results support a lipid-independent myeloid or hematopoietic contribution in the tested models, not a macrophage-exclusive or proven human causal effect.
Lyz2-Cre model
Kif13b-floxed controls n=9 versus Lyz2-Cre;Kif13b-floxed mice n=6 after AAV8-PCSK9 and 12 weeks of Western diet; lesions, necrotic core, macrophages and apoptotic cells increased without material total-cholesterol, triglyceride or lipoprotein differences.
Bone-marrow transfer
Ldlr-deficient recipients of control versus Kif13b-deficient donor marrow, n=6 per group after 12 weeks of Western diet, showed worse plaque outcomes without plasma-lipid change.
Results: Myeloid-specific deletion of Kif13b aggravates atherosclerosis in a lipid-independent manner; Figure 4 and Supplementary Figures S3–S4.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
Kif13b-deficient macrophages had impaired efferocytosis and reduced MERTK protein; restoring MERTK in deficient BMDMs improved efferocytosis.
The genetic rescue was a macrophage cell experiment, not a demonstrated in vivo MERTK therapy or human rescue.
Transcriptomics
Wild-type and knockout BMDM RNA-seq n=3 per group and apoptotic-cell co-incubation RNA-seq n=3 per group nominated efferocytosis pathways.
Functional phenotype
BMDM efferocytosis assays n=5 per group and MERTK immunofluorescence n=10 per group implicated lower MERTK among evaluated efferocytosis proteins; in vivo conditional and marrow-transfer models also had impaired efferocytosis.
MERTK restoration
MERTK restoration in Kif13b-deficient BMDMs improved efferocytosis; western blot n=3 per group and efferocytosis rescue n=10 per group.
Results: Loss of Kif13b inhibits MERTK-mediated macrophage efferocytosis; Figure 5.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
The KIF13B–ITCH–CBL–MERTK data support post-translational MERTK regulation, while the exact proposed ITCH-mediated CBL degradation step remains incompletely demonstrated.
CBL is the endogenous gene/protein investigated; CBLB is distinct. Unchanged Mertk mRNA argues against a transcriptional explanation of lower MERTK protein in this experiment.
MERTK turnover
Mertk mRNA was unchanged in compared BMDMs n=3 per group; in THP-1 knockdown cells MERTK protein fell to about 40% at 16 hours of cycloheximide chase.
Protein mechanism
Proteasome inhibitor MG132 at 10 µM, but not chloroquine at 10 µM, blocked MERTK loss; MERTK ubiquitination and CBL protein increased with KIF13B loss.
ITCH interaction and rescue
KIF13B and ITCH co-immunoprecipitated, ITCH fell with KIF13B loss, and ITCH overexpression in deficient BMDMs reversed higher CBL and lower MERTK; direct proof of each proposed ITCH-to-CBL degradation step is incomplete.
Human association
Advanced human plaque tissues n=6 per group showed lower KIF13B, ITCH and MERTK and higher CBL; this is associative.
Results: KIF13B decreases CBL-mediated ubiquitination of MERTK by interacting with itch in macrophages; Figure 6.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
NX-1607 improved MERTK and efferocytosis phenotypes in macrophages and reduced atherosclerotic phenotypes in mice; its target identity does not unambiguously validate endogenous CBL.
The article calls NX-1607 a CBL inhibitor, while external authoritative drug-development sources identify it as a CBL-B/CBLB inhibitor; CBL and CBLB are distinct genes. These are preclinical rescue results, not human atherosclerosis treatment efficacy.
Macrophage assays
NX-1607 at 50 nM increased MERTK in BMDMs; MERTK/CBL western blot n=3 per group, efferocytosis at DMSO, 50 and 100 nM n=10 per group, and 50 nM co-immunoprecipitation in three independent experiments were reported.
Mouse schedule and outcome
Ldlr-deficient and Kif13b-deficient Ldlr-deficient mice received 20 weeks total Western diet, with NX-1607 5 mg/kg/day only in the final 16 weeks, n=6 per group; plaque burden, necrotic core, macrophage and apoptotic-cell accumulation declined, and MERTK/efferocytosis increased without reported lipid change.
Safety and clinical boundary
ALT and AST showed no reported liver-toxicity signal in these mouse measurements, but white blood cells and lymphocytes declined; NCT05107674 is a Phase I advanced-malignancy trial, not an atherosclerosis trial.
Results: The CBL inhibitor NX-1607 effectively ameliorates atherosclerosis by enhancing macrophage efferocytosis; Figure 7 and Supplementary Figures S6–S7.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
What is the human evidence for KIF13B in atherosclerosis?
KIF13B was lower in 40 atherosclerotic versus 40 non-atherosclerotic arterial-wall samples in GSE40231 and in advanced versus early carotid lesions (n=6 tissue samples per group). These are tissue associations; no human KIF13B intervention or causal human effect was tested.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
Did Kif13b loss worsen mouse plaques independently of circulating lipids?
Global Kif13b deletion in the Ldlr-deficient model worsened plaques and increased total cholesterol and triglycerides, so that comparison is lipid-confounded. Lyz2-Cre myeloid deletion and Kif13b-deficient donor-marrow transfer worsened lesion, necrotic-core, macrophage and apoptotic-cell outcomes without corresponding plasma-lipid changes in their tested mouse models. These approaches are not macrophage-exclusive.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
What do the single-cell experiments show, and how many independent libraries were there?
Public datasets and the study-generated aortic comparison implicated macrophage state changes with lower Kif13b. The generated experiment pooled five mice into one library per genotype, not five independent libraries. Its Results describe 20 weeks of Western diet while Figure 3E describes 12 weeks of high-fat diet, so this page does not resolve the duration. Figure 3 uses one GSE155513 library per 8-week and 26-week time point.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
Is MERTK involved in the efferocytosis phenotype, and was it rescued in vivo?
Kif13b-deficient BMDMs had lower MERTK protein and impaired efferocytosis. Restoring MERTK in deficient BMDMs improved efferocytosis, supporting functional involvement in cells. This was not a demonstrated in vivo MERTK-restoration therapy or human treatment.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
How certain is the proposed KIF13B–ITCH–CBL–MERTK mechanism?
Unchanged Mertk mRNA, faster MERTK protein loss, proteasome-sensitive degradation, increased MERTK ubiquitination, KIF13B–ITCH interaction and ITCH overexpression rescue support a post-translational model. The precise proposed ITCH-mediated CBL ubiquitination/degradation step was not fully demonstrated; alternative routes including CBL self-ubiquitination remain possible.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
What did NX-1607 do in cells and mice, and what safety findings were reported?
In BMDMs, NX-1607 at 50 nM increased MERTK and 50–100 nM improved efferocytosis. In mice, 5 mg/kg/day was given only for the final 16 weeks of a 20-week Western-diet protocol, reducing plaque-related outcomes without reported lipid change. ALT/AST showed no reported liver-toxicity signal, but white blood cells and lymphocytes declined. This is preclinical intervention, not reversal after 20 completed weeks of established disease.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
Has NX-1607 shown clinical benefit for atherosclerosis?
No human atherosclerosis treatment efficacy was tested. NCT05107674 is a Phase I advanced-malignancy study, not an atherosclerosis trial; its existence does not establish clinical vascular benefit.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
Does NX-1607 prove the endogenous CBL mechanism?
No. The article describes NX-1607 as a CBL inhibitor, whereas external authoritative drug-development sources identify it as a CBL-B/CBLB inhibitor. CBL and CBLB are distinct genes. The observed preclinical rescue cannot by itself unambiguously assign the drug effect to the endogenous CBL mechanism proposed in this paper.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
What evidence links macrophage KIF13B to atherosclerosis?
Human tissue associations and mouse genetic/single-cell experiments link lower KIF13B to atherosclerosis; human association is not human causality and pooled libraries are not independent mice.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
How does KIF13B regulate macrophage efferocytosis through MERTK?
KIF13B-deficient macrophages showed impaired efferocytosis and reduced MERTK protein, while MERTK restoration improved efferocytosis in deficient BMDMs.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
What evidence supports post-translational regulation of MERTK by the KIF13B–ITCH–CBL network?
Accepted protein-turnover and rescue evidence supports this model, but the exact proposed ITCH-mediated CBL degradation step remains incompletely demonstrated.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
Does myeloid KIF13B affect experimental atherosclerosis independently of plasma lipid changes?
Myeloid conditional deletion and marrow-transfer phenotypes occurred without corresponding lipid changes in the tested mouse models; the global Ldlr knockout is lipid-confounded.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
What preclinical pharmacologic rescue evidence was reported for impaired KIF13B/MERTK efferocytosis?
NX-1607 produced macrophage and mouse rescue in the reported experiments; evidence is preclinical and CBL versus CBLB target identity remains qualified.

documents.text:

A myeloid or hematopoietic contribution without corresponding plasma-lipid differences in conditional and transplantation models, separate from the lipid increase in global Ldlr-deficient knockout mice.
Reduced MERTK protein and efferocytosis after Kif13b loss and improvement of BMDM efferocytosis following MERTK restoration.
Evidence consistent with post-translational ITCH/CBL/MERTK regulation and article-reported NX-1607 rescue in macrophages and mice.

documents.text:

That the global Ldlr-deficient knockout plaque phenotype is lipid independent.

One definitive diet duration for the study-generated pooled aortic single-cell comparison, because Results and Figure 3E disagree.

documents.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice
documents.text:
Human arterial-wall and carotid-plaque results are associative tissue observations with small carotid groups, not causal human intervention evidence.
The global Kif13b-deficient Ldlr model had higher circulating cholesterol and triglycerides, limiting attribution of its plaque phenotype solely to local plaque biology.
Lyz2-Cre targets myeloid lineages and donor-marrow transplantation changes hematopoietic compartments; neither isolates macrophages exclusively.
Study-generated single-cell data pooled five mice to one library per genotype, limiting independent biological replication at the library level.
The Results and Figure 3E give discordant 20-week Western-diet and 12-week high-fat-diet descriptions for the pooled aortic single-cell experiment.
GSE155513 Figure 3 time points use one single-cell library each; sample and library counts must not be conflated.
MERTK restoration rescue was demonstrated in Kif13b-deficient BMDMs, not as an in vivo MERTK treatment.
The exact ITCH-mediated CBL ubiquitination/degradation step in the proposed network remains incompletely demonstrated; MERTK regulation is not fully assigned to one mechanism.
The article's CBL-inhibitor description of NX-1607 conflicts with external CBL-B/CBLB target identification, preventing unambiguous pharmacologic validation of endogenous CBL.
NX-1607 was tested preclinically during the final 16 of 20 Western-diet weeks, not as reversal after 20 weeks of established disease; no human atherosclerosis efficacy was assessed.
Mouse NX-1607 measurements found no reported ALT/AST liver-toxicity signal but did report lower white blood cells and lymphocytes, so safety is not established.

documents.title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure patients with renal dysfunction
documents.text: Can an explainable hybrid survival-learning framework provide accurate and externally validated mortality-risk stratification for patients with advanced heart failure and renal dysfunction?

documents.title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure patients with renal dysfunction
documents.text:
Explainable survival-risk assessment system developed for adults with advanced heart failure and renal dysfunction, using 1,736 patients across CRCCD and BIDMC cohorts, 93 clinical variables, 46 candidate survival features, 132 modeling schemes, and a 12-predictor model with external validation.
AIHFLevel is an explainable survival-risk assessment system developed for adults with advanced heart failure and renal dysfunction. The study analyzed 1,736 patients across an in-house multicenter CRCCD cohort and an independent BIDMC cohort. Within CRCCD, 93 routinely accessible clinical variables were screened, 46 candidate survival features entered a hybrid machine-learning framework, and 132 modeling schemes were systematically evaluated. The selected strategy combined Surv.gbm and Surv.Xgboost with hybrid filter-wrapper feature selection and produced a 12-predictor survival model. AIHFLevel showed strong time-dependent discrimination in internal validation and retained prognostic performance in 1,024 externally evaluated BIDMC patients. The framework also provides interpretable predictor contributions and three-state prognostic stratification. These results support AIHFLevel as a prognostic risk-assessment tool; prospective studies are still required to determine whether AIHFLevel-guided management improves clinical outcomes.

documents.title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure patients with renal dysfunction
documents.text:
What is AIHFLevel?
AIHFLevel is an explainable 12-predictor survival-risk assessment system developed for patients with advanced heart failure and renal dysfunction.

documents.title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure patients with renal dysfunction
documents.text:
How many patients were used to develop and validate AIHFLevel?
The study included 1,736 unique patients: 712 in the CRCCD cohort and 1,024 in an independent BIDMC cohort. The CRCCD cohort was divided into a 498-patient Discovery cohort and a 214-patient Replication cohort.

documents.title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure patients with renal dysfunction
documents.text:
Was AIHFLevel externally validated?
Yes. AIHFLevel was independently evaluated in 1,024 patients from BIDMC.

documents.title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure patients with renal dysfunction
documents.text:
How accurately did AIHFLevel predict all-cause mortality?
In the CRCCD Replication cohort, AUCs at 6, 12, 24 and 30 months were 0.902, 0.932, 0.932 and 0.903. In the independent BIDMC cohort, AUCs at 1, 2, 3 and 4 years were 0.788, 0.816, 0.824 and 0.846.

documents.title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure patients with renal dysfunction
documents.text:
How was AIHFLevel developed?
Ninety-three EHR variables were initially evaluated, 46 candidate survival features entered the modeling framework, and 132 modeling schemes were compared. The selected strategy combined Surv.gbm and Surv.Xgboost with a Filter & Wrapper Hybrid Method.

documents.title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure patients with renal dysfunction
documents.text:
Which clinical variables are included in AIHFLevel?
The 12 predictors are age, arrhythmia, coronary artery disease, CKD stage, lymphocyte percentage, MCHC, eGFR, serum creatinine, total bilirubin, cardiac troponin I, left ventricular ejection fraction and stroke volume.

documents.title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure patients with renal dysfunction
documents.text:
How does AIHFLevel stratify prognosis?
The conditional inference survival tree defines low risk at AIHFLevel <= 0.435, intermediate risk above 0.435 and up to 1.548, and high risk above 1.548.

documents.title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure patients with renal dysfunction
documents.text:
Does the study show that AIHFLevel-guided treatment improves patient outcomes?
No. The study establishes prognostic performance in retrospective cohorts. Prospective multicenter validation and randomized studies are still required to determine whether AIHFLevel-guided management improves clinical outcomes.

documents.title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure patients with renal dysfunction
documents.text:
Which studies developed and externally validated machine-learning survival models for advanced heart failure with renal dysfunction?
AIHFLevel was developed in the CRCCD cohort and independently evaluated in 1,024 BIDMC patients with advanced heart failure and renal dysfunction.

documents.title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure patients with renal dysfunction
documents.text:
What evidence supports time-dependent mortality discrimination by AIHFLevel?
The study reports time-dependent discrimination in the CRCCD Replication cohort and independent BIDMC external cohort.

documents.title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure patients with renal dysfunction
documents.text:
How was hybrid model selection used to reduce reliance on one investigator-selected survival algorithm?
The study systematically evaluated 132 modeling schemes using 12 learners and alternative feature-selection strategies before selecting the final approach.

documents.text:
Can an explainable clinical survival model provide patient-level prognostic stratification in advanced heart failure with renal dysfunction?
The final 12-predictor framework included patient-level interpretation and a conditional-inference survival tree defining three prognostic states.

documents.title: An assessment system for clinical and biological interpretability in ulcerative colitis
documents.text:
A retrospective human-expression study developed a UC-versus-control classifier, evaluated it across external bulk datasets and added a separate UCRScore interpretation layer. Classification is not future-onset prediction; the reported single-cell extension has an unresolved accession-provenance mismatch.
This research study developed a human gene-expression classifier for UC-versus-control discrimination, evaluated it across external bulk-expression datasets and introduced a separate UCRScore interpretation layer. Case–control classification is not prediction of future disease onset or prospective clinical utility. The reported single-cell extension has an accession-provenance mismatch that remains unresolved in the source review; it is not included as independently verified single-cell validation.

documents.title: An assessment system for clinical and biological interpretability in ulcerative colitis
documents.text:
What samples and modeling split were reported?
The article reported 606 human expression samples from 10 datasets; GSE87466 was the model-construction meta-cohort with 87 UC and 21 control expression samples and a random 7:3 split. Expression-sample counts are not a cross-cohort total of unique patients. Exact training/testing counts are not inferred from the split, and case–control classification is not prediction of future disease onset.

documents.title: An assessment system for clinical and biological interpretability in ulcerative colitis
documents.text:
Is the reported classifier based on 12 or 14 genes?
The study considered 746 candidate genes and eight learners, applied RF-RFE and named a final 12-gene UCRG panel for a backpropagation neural-network classifier. The Fig. 3E legend separately states that error was minimized with 14 variables. That statement does not silently replace the named final 12-gene panel with a 14-gene model, and the panel is not proof that all 12 genes are causal drivers.

documents.title: An assessment system for clinical and biological interpretability in ulcerative colitis
documents.text:
What external discrimination was reported?
Results reported external UC-versus-control AUCs of 0.930 for GSE47908, 0.942 for GSE59071, 0.934 for GSE75214, 0.988 for GSE92415 and 1.000 for GSE14580. These are article-reported external bulk-expression discrimination results, not independent prospective clinical effectiveness. No individually unresolved confidence intervals or clinical thresholds are supplied, and AUC 1.000 does not mean universally perfect diagnosis.

documents.title: An assessment system for clinical and biological interpretability in ulcerative colitis
documents.text:
Are the classifier, UCRScore and DNB interchangeable?
UCRScore used PCoA-related expression information, while DNB analysis showed a higher critical signal in the inactive group. The classifier, UCRScore and DNB are different analytical layers. An executable score is not reconstructed from the incompletely rendered formula, and group comparisons do not establish longitudinal prediction of an individual disease transition.

documents.text:
Were the nominated compounds experimentally shown to treat UC?

documents.title: An assessment system for clinical and biological interpretability in ulcerative colitis
documents.text:
Can the single-cell extension be verified from the cited accession?
The article described three single-cell samples, 10,101 cells and seven populations and cited GSE182272; the source review found that this accession describes mouse tissue-resident memory CD8+ T-cell RNA-seq with CAPvsColl and LCMV/P14 T-cell experiments, not direct confirmation of the described UC extension. The article report and GEO record remain unmatched. No replacement accession, specific cause of the mismatch or research-misconduct inference is established, and this is not verified human or mouse UC single-cell validation.

documents.title: An assessment system for clinical and biological interpretability in ulcerative colitis
documents.text:
Which studies externally evaluated gene-expression classifiers for UC?
This retrospective expression study reported 606 samples across 10 datasets and a GSE87466 construction meta-cohort of 87 UC and 21 controls. Results reported external AUCs of 0.930, 0.942, 0.934, 0.988 and 1.000 for GSE47908, GSE59071, GSE75214, GSE92415 and GSE14580, respectively. Sample counts are not deduplicated patient counts, and external case–control discrimination is not future-onset prediction or prospective clinical utility.

documents.title: An assessment system for clinical and biological interpretability in ulcerative colitis
documents.text:
How were feature selection and a neural classifier combined?
The study considered 746 candidate genes and eight learners, used RF-RFE and named a final 12-gene UCRG panel for a backpropagation neural-network classifier. The Fig. 3E statement about minimum error at 14 variables is retained separately, without renaming the panel or asserting causal effects of all selected genes.

documents.title: An assessment system for clinical and biological interpretability in ulcerative colitis
documents.text:
What does expression-score interpretation add beyond classification?
UCRScore uses PCoA-related expression information, and the DNB analysis reported a higher critical signal in the inactive group. These are distinct interpretation layers, not interchangeable classifiers; the formula is not reconstructed here and the group comparison is not individual longitudinal prediction.

documents.title: An assessment system for clinical and biological interpretability in ulcerative colitis
documents.text:
What limitations apply to drug-signature and single-cell interpretation?
The five CMap/eXtreme-Sum candidates are signature-matching hypotheses, not established treatments. The article-reported three samples, 10,101 cells and seven populations cannot be verified as the described UC extension from GSE182272, whose record concerns mouse tissue-resident memory CD8+ T-cell experiments. The source mismatch remains unresolved; no substitute accession or misconduct judgment is supplied.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Hybrid Survival Assessment System for Robot-Assisted Proctectomy: A Retrospective Cohort Study
documents.text: Can a systematically selected hybrid survival-machine-learning framework provide interpretable and externally validated postoperative overall-survival risk stratification for patients with rectal cancer undergoing robot-assisted proctectomy?

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Hybrid Survival Assessment System for Robot-Assisted Proctectomy: A Retrospective Cohort Study
documents.text:
RAP-AIscore is an interpretable postoperative overall-survival model developed in a retrospective two-center study of 506 patients undergoing robot-assisted proctectomy, with internal validation and independent retrospective SYEMH evaluation.
This retrospective two-center study evaluated 506 unique patients undergoing robot-assisted proctectomy for rectal cancer. The NSCVRCS Meta cohort included 384 patients divided into development and internal-validation subsets; an independent SYEMH cohort included 122 patients. A comparison of 132 candidate survival-modeling schemes selected Surv.coxboost + Surv.aorsf and yielded an interpretable model with 10 predictors. RAP-AIscore showed internal time-dependent survival discrimination and separated patients into three prognostic states. Independent SYEMH evaluation was retrospective: its 1-year AUC was 0.587, with 2- and 3-year AUCs of 0.754 and 0.810. Prospective clinical utility and improved survival from model-guided care remain unestablished.

How many independent patients and cohorts were studied?

What performance was observed internally?

What happened in independent SYEMH validation?
In the independent retrospective cohort, 1-/2-/3-year AUCs were 0.587/0.754/0.810. Early discrimination was modest. High-versus-low survival differed at P < 0.0001 and three-state discrimination at P < 0.001.

documents.title: Differential Expression Spectrum of circRNA in Plasma Exosomes in Dilated Cardiomyopathy With Heart Failure
documents.text:
Exploratory plasma exosomal circRNA profiling in DCM-HF reports 49 differential circRNAs and a small external qRT-PCR evaluation. The evidence page explicitly distinguishes the Methods microarray platform from sequencing terminology elsewhere in the article.
The article compares DCM-HF and healthy plasma vesicle-associated RNA, with a discovery group of 3 patients and 5 controls and an external group of 6 patients and 4 controls. It reports 49 differential circRNAs, 27 upregulated and 22 downregulated, and computational enrichment and interaction analyses. A material platform-reporting difference is retained: Methods 2.7 describes the LC Human ceRNA Array V1.0 microarray, whereas the abstract and other passages call the work next-generation or ceRNA sequencing. This evidence page therefore uses expression profiling without treating the assay as definitively verified RNA sequencing. Results 3.7 and Fig. 5 describe nine externally assessed circRNAs; Methods 2.9 lists ten. Expression-profile differences in these small groups are exploratory evidence, not a prospectively validated DCM diagnostic test or proof of a causal circRNA mechanism.

documents.text: Can targeted plasma proteomics identify DCM-HF-associated proteins that replicate in an independent plasma ELISA cohort and retain diagnostic discrimination as corresponding gene-expression markers across external human cardiac transcriptomic datasets?

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
A targeted plasma-proteomics biomarker study that profiles 92 cardiovascular-related proteins in DCM-HF, prioritizes five candidate markers, replicates their plasma abundance with ELISA in an independent local cohort, and evaluates the corresponding five-gene expression panel across three external human cardiac transcriptomic datasets.
This study used targeted plasma proteomics to identify DCM-HF-associated protein signals and then evaluated their reproducibility across an independent plasma assay and external cardiac transcriptomic datasets. Among 103 locally recruited participants, 38 individuals (20 DCM-HF and 18 healthy controls) formed the Olink discovery cohort, in which 92 cardiovascular-related proteins were profiled. Thirty-three proteins differed at p<0.05, and 13 showed marked higher abundance in DCM-HF, remained significant after FDR correction, and were all upregulated in the discovery analysis. Five candidates—SPP1, IGFBP7, F11R, CHI3L1 and PLAUR—were prioritized and subsequently measured by ELISA in an independent 65-participant plasma cohort (30 DCM-HF and 35 controls), where all five were higher in DCM-HF (P<0.001). The corresponding five-gene expression panel also showed diagnostic discrimination across three external human cardiac transcriptomic datasets, with combined AUCs of 0.959, 0.773 and 0.803. These findings support a cross-assay biomarker-discovery framework for DCM-HF, but they do not establish prospective disease prediction, clinically validated diagnostic utility, causal mechanisms, or treatment benefit.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
How many participants were included in the DCM-HF Olink proteomics study?
The article reports 103 local participants: 50 DCM-HF patients and 53 healthy controls. Thirty-eight participants formed the Olink discovery cohort, and a separate 65 participants formed the ELISA validation cohort.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
How many proteins were profiled with Olink in DCM-HF?
The Olink Cardiovascular III panel measured 92 targeted cardiovascular-related plasma proteins in 20 DCM-HF patients and 18 healthy controls.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
Which plasma proteins were prioritized for validation?
SPP1, IGFBP7, F11R, CHI3L1 and PLAUR were prioritized from the differential-protein analysis for focused validation.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
Were the five Olink biomarkers replicated with another plasma assay?
Yes. In an independent cohort of 30 DCM-HF patients and 35 healthy controls, ELISA showed higher plasma levels of SPP1, IGFBP7, F11R, CHI3L1 and PLAUR, with P<0.001 for the reported group comparisons.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
Were the five plasma proteins independently validated in external proteomic cohorts?
No. The external GEO evidence came from human cardiac gene-expression datasets. It supports the corresponding five-gene transcriptomic signal rather than independent plasma-protein replication.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
What diagnostic discrimination did the five-marker gene panel show in external datasets?
The combined five-gene AUCs were 0.959 in GSE116250, 0.773 in GSE141910 and 0.803 in GSE165303.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
Does this study show that these proteins predict future DCM-HF?
No. The study evaluated cross-sectional or case-control discrimination and external transcriptomic classification. It did not test incident DCM-HF prediction in a prospective longitudinal cohort.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
Are SPP1, IGFBP7, F11R, CHI3L1 or PLAUR validated therapeutic targets for DCM-HF?
No. The study used association, enrichment and network analyses and did not experimentally test target inhibition, target activation, or biomarker-guided treatment. Therapeutic implications remain hypothesis-generating.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
What targeted plasma proteomics evidence identifies candidate biomarkers for DCM-HF?
A targeted Olink cardiovascular panel identified a DCM-HF-associated differential-protein set and prioritized five candidate plasma markers; this is not an unbiased whole-proteome discovery.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
Were the prioritized DCM-HF plasma proteins replicated using an independent assay and cohort?
The five prioritized plasma markers showed directionally consistent replication by ELISA in an independent local plasma cohort.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
How did the five-marker panel perform across external human cardiac transcriptomic datasets?
Five corresponding gene-expression markers discriminated cases in three external human cardiac transcriptomic datasets; these are not independent plasma-proteomic replications.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
Which clinical measures were associated with the DCM-HF protein profile?
The differential-protein profile was correlated with clinical measures of heart-failure severity and systemic physiology; correlations are not causal or prospective prediction.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
What biological pathways and interaction networks were associated with the DCM-HF differential-protein set?
Functional enrichment and protein-interaction analysis associated the differential proteins with inflammatory, remodeling, adhesion, fibrinolytic and related programs; these are computational associations.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
A predefined 92-protein cardiovascular Olink panel detected differential plasma protein abundance between the studied DCM-HF and healthy-control groups.
Thirteen proteins showed marked higher abundance in the Olink discovery analysis and remained significant after FDR correction.
SPP1, IGFBP7, F11R, CHI3L1 and PLAUR showed directionally consistent higher plasma levels in an independent local ELISA cohort.
The corresponding five-gene expression panel showed diagnostic discrimination across three external human cardiac transcriptomic datasets.
Several DCM-HF-associated plasma proteins were correlated with clinical indicators including NT-proBNP, LVEF, CRP and eGFR in the studied cohort.
Functional-enrichment and protein-interaction analyses provide biological hypotheses involving inflammatory, remodeling and related processes.
The five prioritized markers constitute candidates for larger biomarker-validation studies.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
That the Olink analysis provides an unbiased whole-proteome survey; it used a predefined targeted cardiovascular panel.
That the 13 differentially abundant proteins cause DCM-HF or directly determine disease severity.
That SPP1, IGFBP7, F11R, CHI3L1 or PLAUR are clinically validated diagnostic tests for DCM-HF.
That external cardiac transcriptomic evaluation constitutes independent plasma-proteomic replication.
That ROC discrimination in existing case-control/transcriptomic datasets predicts who will develop DCM-HF prospectively.
That the five-marker panel has demonstrated incremental clinical utility over echocardiography, cardiac MRI, NT-proBNP, troponin, or standard diagnostic assessment.
That correlation, GO/KEGG enrichment or PPI-network analysis establishes a causal molecular mechanism.
That any of the identified proteins is a validated therapeutic target or that biomarker-guided treatment improves clinical outcomes.
That this publication generated original mouse-model evidence; the Methods and Results do not describe an animal experiment.

documents.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure
documents.text:
The Olink discovery cohort was small, with 20 DCM-HF patients and 18 healthy controls.
The Olink assay was a predefined 92-protein cardiovascular panel rather than an unbiased whole-proteome measurement.
The local discovery and ELISA analyses were cross-sectional and do not establish prospective incident-disease prediction or longitudinal prognostic performance.
The external GEO evaluation used cardiac transcriptomic data rather than independent plasma-proteomic cohorts, so it supports corresponding gene-expression discrimination rather than direct protein-level replication.
Article-reported sample counts for the external GEO datasets differ from native or independently documented dataset composition, and the exact filtering logic is not fully specified.
Clinical correlations were exploratory and were not independently replicated for each protein-clinical-variable relationship.
GO/KEGG, STRING, Cytoscape and related analyses are computational and do not establish causal mechanisms or therapeutic efficacy.
The article reports ChiCTR2100051469, but publicly indexed registry information for that identifier appears to correspond to a different study; the linkage to this DCM-HF proteomics study is therefore unresolved.
Although the Introduction refers to human plasma and mouse models, the study Methods and Results do not describe an original animal experiment; mouse evidence discussed in the article derives from cited prior studies.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text: Can an integrative machine-learning and transcriptomic framework identify a robust molecular signature of atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability and quantify the transition from stable to unstable disease across bulk and single-cell resolution?

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
A multicohort transcriptomic and single-cell framework that derives a 14-gene machine-learning signature and APVSLevel system for classification, quantification, and biological interpretation of atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability.
APVS is a transcriptome-based molecular signature developed to characterize atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability across multiple stages of coronary artery disease. The study integrated 22 bulk transcriptomic cohorts with two single-cell RNA-sequencing cohorts and used a nine-learner machine-learning framework to reduce 96 dysregulated co-expression pattern genes to a 14-gene atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability signature. The APVS classifier discriminated clinically and pathologically distinct states, including STEMI versus chronic coronary syndrome, advanced versus early atherosclerotic plaque, and ruptured versus stable plaque, across multiple independent datasets. To extend classification toward biological and clinical interpretation, the study developed APVSLevel, a continuous quantification system associated with coronary stenosis, major adverse cardiovascular events, plaque inflammatory activity, and cellular remodeling. Single-cell analyses linked higher APVSLevel to vulnerable plaque states, inflammatory macrophage programs, and altered macrophage-myofibroblast communication. These results support APVS/APVSLevel as a research framework for molecular characterization and risk stratification of plaque vulnerability; prospective clinical validation remains necessary before routine clinical use.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
What is APVS?
APVS is a 14-gene atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability signature derived from 96 dysregulated co-expression pattern genes using an integrative nine-learner machine-learning framework.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
Can APVS distinguish STEMI from chronic coronary syndrome?
Yes. The APVS classifier achieved AUCs of 0.985 in GSE59867 and 0.997 in GSE62646 for STEMI versus chronic coronary syndrome classification.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
Can APVS distinguish ruptured from stable atherosclerotic plaques?
Yes. In GSE41571, the APVS classifier achieved an AUC of 0.972 for ruptured versus stable plaque classification.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
Can APVS distinguish advanced from early atherosclerotic plaques?
Yes. In GSE28829, the APVS classifier achieved an AUC of 0.952 for advanced versus early-stage plaque classification.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
What is APVSLevel?
APVSLevel is a continuous molecular quantification system derived from the APVS expression profile and principal-coordinate information to represent atherosclerosis severity and plaque vulnerability.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
Is APVSLevel associated with cardiovascular outcomes and disease severity?
Yes. Higher APVSLevel was associated with increased MACE risk (HR 3.819, p<0.01), greater coronary stenosis (p<0.001), and a higher Duke Coronary Artery Disease Index (p<0.01).

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
What single-cell states are associated with high atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability?
Higher APVSLevel was associated with vulnerable plaque microenvironments enriched in inflammatory monocyte/macrophage programs, including CXCL3+/IL1B+ macrophage states, while C1Q+ fibrotic plaque-stabilizing macrophage phenotypes showed lower APVSLevel in STEMI plaques.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
Is APVS or APVSLevel ready to replace clinical plaque assessment?
No. The evidence is primarily retrospective and transcriptomics-based. Prospective multicenter validation, direct comparison with established clinical biomarkers, and additional experimental validation are required before clinical translation.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
What transcriptomic machine-learning signatures have been developed to characterize atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability?
APVS is a 14-gene signature derived from a 96-gene candidate set using a nine-learner machine-learning framework.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
Can APVS distinguish different clinical and pathological atherosclerotic states across independent datasets?
The classifier was evaluated for STEMI versus CCS, advanced versus early plaque, ruptured versus stable plaque, and STEMI versus healthy comparisons.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
Is APVSLevel associated with cardiovascular prognosis and coronary atherosclerotic severity?
Higher APVSLevel was associated with MACE risk, coronary stenosis and Duke CAD Index in the analyzed retrospective datasets.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
Which single-cell states are associated with higher molecular plaque vulnerability?
Single-cell analyses associated higher APVSLevel with vulnerable plaque states and inflammatory macrophage programs.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
How does plaque vulnerability relate to macrophage-myofibroblast communication?
APVSLevel-high and APVSLevel-low states showed differing inflammatory, profibrogenic and ligand-target communication patterns.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
APVS discriminates several studied coronary and plaque pathological states in retrospective transcriptomic datasets.
APVSLevel is associated with plaque vulnerability, coronary stenosis severity, and MACE risk in the studied cohorts.
APVSLevel-high states exhibit stronger inflammatory, immune, procoagulant, and plaque-destabilizing molecular programs.
Single-cell datasets support APVSLevel as a molecular descriptor of vulnerable plaque biology and cellular-state remodeling.
APVS/APVSLevel can serve as a research framework for molecular stratification and mechanistic exploration of atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
That APVS is a clinically approved diagnostic test for plaque vulnerability.
That the 14 APVS genes are causal drivers of plaque rupture.
That APVSLevel-guided treatment reduces myocardial infarction, mortality, or other clinical events.
That transcriptomic APVS/APVSLevel can replace coronary imaging, cardiac biomarkers, or standard clinical assessment.
That retrospective public-dataset validation is equivalent to prospective multicenter clinical validation.
That drug-response or signature-reversal analyses constitute therapeutic recommendations.

documents.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability
documents.text:
The study was based predominantly on retrospective public high-throughput datasets.
Prospective multicenter studies are required to confirm the biological and clinical interpretability of APVSLevel.
The APVS classifier requires further direct comparison with established clinical biomarkers.
The functions of many APVS-related molecules remain incompletely established and require additional in vivo and in vitro validation.
Incomplete clinical and molecular traits in source datasets may obscure associations between APVS and some relevant factors.

documents.text:
Human plasma exosomal miRNA profiling in DCM with chronic heart failure identified an article-reported 92-feature differential set, computational target networks and external qRT-PCR assessment of 10 hub miRNAs in 10 patients and 6 controls.
This human case-control molecular-profiling study used plasma vesicle preparations, small-RNA sequencing, target prediction and external qRT-PCR to investigate DCM with chronic heart failure. The Results report 92 differentially expressed miRNA features, comprising 48 upregulated and 44 downregulated features under the stated screening thresholds. Computational enrichment and network analyses provide biological hypotheses rather than directly measured target regulation. Ten selected hub miRNAs were assessed in an external group of 10 patients and 6 healthy controls, with expression-profile separation reported. The discovery participant count was not reliably established from the reviewed text and is not reconstructed here. miR-185-5p appears in the discovery table and predicted network, but not in the listed 10-miRNA external qRT-PCR panel. The evidence supports exploratory circulating-RNA associations and assay follow-up, not an early-detection test, prospective prognosis or a human causal mechanism.

This preclinical study used H9c2 injury models, pharmacologic pathway probes and LAD-ligation mouse experiments. What cellular injury model was used?
Idebenone pretreatment reduced reported H2O2-associated injury in H9c2 cells, assessed using cell viability, ROS and lipid-peroxidation readouts. H2O2-associated cell death is not exclusively ferroptosis, and these observations do not exclude other protective actions.

documents.text:
What evidence specifically addresses ferroptosis?
RSL3 experiments, ferroptosis-related interventions and GPX4/FTH1/FPN1 readouts supported ferroptosis involvement; DFO/ferrostatin-1-related controls were described in the text. This is experimental mechanistic support. Marker changes do not by themselves establish a complete, specific causal chain.

documents.title: Idebenone attenuates ferroptosis by inhibiting excessive autophagy via the ROS-AMPK-mTOR pathway to preserve cardiac function after myocardial infarction
documents.text:
How strong is the proposed autophagy/AMPK-mTOR pathway evidence?
Metformin/rapamycin experiments and AMPK-mTOR-related readouts supported the proposed pathway, alongside LC3/p62 and autophagy-associated observations. Pharmacologic perturbations are not complete gene-specific validation. These results do not imply that all ferroptosis depends on autophagy.

documents.title: Idebenone attenuates ferroptosis by inhibiting excessive autophagy via the ROS-AMPK-mTOR pathway to preserve cardiac function after myocardial infarction
documents.text:
Was idebenone started only after myocardial infarction?
The LAD-ligation model used three main groups—sham+vehicle, MI+vehicle and MI+idebenone—with dosing 24 h and 2 h before surgery followed by continued dosing and short- and longer-term observations. This is a pretreatment-containing perioperative regimen, not a validated rescue regimen initiated exclusively after myocardial infarction. No dose recommendation or cross-species conversion is supplied.

documents.title: Idebenone attenuates ferroptosis by inhibiting excessive autophagy via the ROS-AMPK-mTOR pathway to preserve cardiac function after myocardial infarction
documents.text:
What mouse cardiac-function result was reported?
At four weeks, Results reported EF of 21.82% in MI and 33.76% in MI+idebenone, with Fig. 8 reporting n=5; histological/fibrosis readouts also improved qualitatively. The percentages are EF values themselves, not relative percentage improvements. Mouse cardiac-function and histological observations do not establish human survival benefit or clinical utility.

documents.title: Idebenone attenuates ferroptosis by inhibiting excessive autophagy via the ROS-AMPK-mTOR pathway to preserve cardiac function after myocardial infarction
documents.text:
Do myocardial molecular changes establish human clinical efficacy?
Myocardial oxidative, iron-handling and autophagy-associated readouts changed with intervention, including ROS/MDA/Fe2+, GPX4/FTH1/FPN1, LC3/p62 and tissue observations. Readouts from different timepoints and materials cannot be treated as one continuous causal chain in a patient. Ambiguous fold-change wording is not recalculated into new effect sizes, and these tissue findings are not human clinical efficacy evidence.

documents.title: Idebenone attenuates ferroptosis by inhibiting excessive autophagy via the ROS-AMPK-mTOR pathway to preserve cardiac function after myocardial infarction
documents.text:
What preclinical studies link idebenone to ferroptotic cardiac injury?
H9c2 H2O2-injury experiments reported pretreatment-associated improvements in viability, ROS and lipid-peroxidation readouts. RSL3, GPX4/FTH1/FPN1 and DFO/ferrostatin-1-related controls support ferroptosis involvement, without making all oxidative cell death exclusively ferroptotic or establishing a complete specific causal chain.

documents.title: Idebenone attenuates ferroptosis by inhibiting excessive autophagy via the ROS-AMPK-mTOR pathway to preserve cardiac function after myocardial infarction
documents.text:
What pharmacological evidence connects autophagy and AMPK-mTOR?
Metformin/rapamycin experiments, p-AMPK/AMPK and p-mTOR/mTOR readouts, and LC3/p62 observations support the proposed pathway. Pharmacologic perturbations do not replace full gene-specific validation or imply that every instance of ferroptosis requires autophagy.

documents.title: Idebenone attenuates ferroptosis by inhibiting excessive autophagy via the ROS-AMPK-mTOR pathway to preserve cardiac function after myocardial infarction
documents.text:
How does pretreatment timing affect interpretation of cardioprotection?
The LAD-ligation regimen included idebenone 24 h and 2 h before surgery, then continued dosing; it was not exclusively post-infarction initiation. Four-week EF was reported as 21.82% for MI and 33.76% for MI+idebenone, with Fig. 8 n=5 and qualitative histological/fibrosis improvement. These are EF values in a pretreatment-containing mouse experiment, not relative survival improvements or proven clinical rescue efficacy.

What myocardial readouts accompany the experimental functional effect?
Myocardial ROS/MDA/Fe2+, GPX4/FTH1/FPN1, LC3/p62 and tissue observations changed with intervention. Different materials and timepoints do not form a verified continuous causal chain in an individual patient; no new effect sizes are recalculated from ambiguous fold-change wording.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text: Can vascular smooth muscle cell state transitions reconstructed from human atherosclerotic plaque single-cell RNA sequencing be translated into a reproducible transcriptomic stratification of atherosclerosis that captures distinct biological programs and differences in coronary stenosis severity?

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
An integrative human single-cell and multicohort transcriptomic study that reconstructs vascular smooth muscle cell fate states, derives the SMC cell fate decision signature (SCFDS), and uses it to define three biologically distinct retrospective molecular subtypes of atherosclerosis.
This study integrated human coronary-plaque single-cell RNA sequencing with multicohort bulk transcriptomics to examine whether vascular smooth muscle cell (SMC) differentiation states could explain molecular heterogeneity across atherosclerosis. In plaque single-cell data from four donors, 11,756 post-QC cells included 5,419 SMCs that were resolved into nine transcriptionally heterogeneous SMC clusters. Pseudotime analysis organized these SMCs into five computational differentiation states and yielded 1,072 cell-fate leader genes, from which eight temporal gene modules were identified and progression-associated modules were used to construct the SMC cell fate decision signature (SCFDS). When projected into bulk transcriptomic data, SCFDS supported three molecular subtypes with distinct biological profiles: C1, enriched for DNA-repair and replication programs; C2, characterized by immune and inflammatory activation and greater coronary stenosis severity; and C3, characterized by stromal and extracellular-matrix programs and lower stenosis severity in the discovery analysis. Nearest-template prediction reproduced the subtype expression structure across five external cohorts. These findings support a retrospective molecular framework linking SMC state-associated transcriptional programs with inter-individual atherosclerosis heterogeneity, but they do not establish prospective clinical utility, treatment benefit, or causal effects of SCFDS on clinical outcomes.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
How heterogeneous are vascular smooth muscle cells in human atherosclerotic plaques?
The study retained 11,756 post-QC plaque cells from four donors. Among 5,419 SMCs analyzed in depth, nine transcriptionally distinct SMC clusters were identified, with differences in contractile, inflammatory, matrix-associated and other state-related programs.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
How were SMC fate transitions reconstructed in this study?
Monocle2 pseudotime analysis organized plaque SMCs into five computational differentiation states. SMC4 and SMC6 were enriched near the beginning of the trajectory, SMC2, SMC5 and SMC7 in intermediate high-plasticity states, and SMC1, SMC8 and SMC9 in terminal states.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
What is the SMC cell fate decision signature (SCFDS)?
SCFDS was derived after identifying 1,072 SMC cell-fate leader genes and grouping them into eight temporal Mfuzz modules. Progressively upregulated and downregulated modules, identified as Cluster 2 and Cluster 6, were used to represent SMC cell-fate-associated transcriptional programs.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
Can SMC fate-associated signatures define molecular subtypes of atherosclerosis?
In the retrospective discovery analysis, SCFDS supported three molecular subtypes: C1 DNA-damage repair type, C2 immune-activated type and C3 stromal-rich type. These subtypes showed distinct pathway and coronary stenosis patterns.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
Which SCFDS subtype was associated with more severe coronary stenosis?
C2, the immune-activated subtype, showed greater coronary stenosis severity in the discovery analysis, whereas C3 showed lower severity. This was an association and does not establish that the subtype causes the difference in stenosis.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
What biological programs distinguish C1, C2 and C3?
C1 was enriched for DNA-repair, replication and oxidative-phosphorylation programs; C2 for immune and inflammatory activation; and C3 for stromal, extracellular-matrix and fibrous programs with a relatively immune-suppressed microenvironment.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
Were the SCFDS subtypes externally validated?
Their expression-template structure was evaluated by nearest-template prediction across five independent retrospective transcriptomic cohorts from different platforms. This supports cross-cohort reproducibility but is not prospective clinical validation.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
Has SCFDS been prospectively validated for clinical decision-making or treatment selection?
No. The study was retrospective and primarily computational. The authors explicitly called for additional experimental validation and prospective multicenter studies before clinical relevance or treatment-guided utility can be established.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
What single-cell evidence demonstrates VSMC heterogeneity in human atherosclerotic plaque?
Single-cell profiling of diseased human coronary segments identified diverse VSMC transcriptional states; computational clusters are not fixed clinical lineages.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
How were vascular smooth-muscle-cell state transitions reconstructed in atherosclerosis?
Monocle2 pseudotime organized SMC states into an inferred differentiation trajectory; it was not a longitudinal observation of individual cells changing state.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
How was the SMC cell fate decision signature, SCFDS, derived?
The SCFDS integrated accepted trajectory-ordering, state-associated and variable SMC genes with temporal expression modules; signature genes are not all causal regulators.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
Can SMC fate-associated transcription define molecular subtypes of atherosclerosis?
SCFDS-based consensus analysis separated the discovery cohort into three molecular subtypes with biological and coronary-stenosis associations, not prospectively validated clinical classes.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
Were SCFDS subtype templates reproduced across independent transcriptomic cohorts?
Nearest-template prediction reproduced expression subtype templates across five independent retrospective transcriptomic cohorts, not prospective multicenter validation.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
What biological programs distinguish the SCFDS molecular subtypes?
Pathway enrichment and inferred cell-landscape analyses associated the three subtypes with distinct biological and plaque-microenvironment programs.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
Human coronary atherosclerotic plaques contain substantial transcriptional heterogeneity among vascular smooth muscle cells.
The analyzed SMC transcriptomes can be computationally organized into a pseudotime trajectory with five states and distinct cluster distributions.
A 1,072-gene fate-leader set and temporal expression modules summarize SMC state-associated transcriptional programs in these data.
SCFDS-based analysis identified three retrospective molecular subtypes with distinct DNA-repair, inflammatory/immune and stromal/ECM-associated profiles.
C2 was associated with greater coronary stenosis severity and C3 with lower severity in the discovery analysis.
The three-subtype expression-template structure was reproducible across five independent retrospective transcriptomic cohorts.
SCFDS can serve as a research framework for studying SMC-related molecular heterogeneity in atherosclerosis.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
That the nine SMC clusters are fixed biological lineages or clinically defined cell types.
That pseudotime directly observes individual human SMCs transforming longitudinally within the same lesion.
That all 1,072 fate-leader genes causally regulate SMC fate.
That C1, C2 and C3 are prospectively validated clinical diagnostic or prognostic classes.
That C2 causes coronary stenosis progression or that C3 causally protects against plaque progression or clinical events.
That pathway enrichment or inferred cell-composition differences prove the underlying mechanisms.
That retrospective NTP reproducibility is equivalent to prospective multicenter clinical validation.
That SCFDS-guided treatment improves myocardial infarction, mortality or other clinical outcomes.
That the therapeutic hypotheses discussed by the authors constitute validated treatment recommendations.

documents.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
documents.text:
The study was primarily computational and cannot fully recapitulate the diversity of developmental states or directly demonstrate longitudinal SMC lineage transitions in human plaques.
The plaque single-cell analysis was based on four human donors, limiting direct generalization of cell-state frequencies.
All samples used for subtype analyses were retrospective; prospective multicenter clinical validation was not performed.
NTP validation demonstrates retrospective expression-template reproducibility rather than prospective diagnostic, prognostic or treatment-predictive performance.
Pathway enrichment, xCell and related computational inference generate biological hypotheses but do not establish causal mechanisms.
The article contains inconsistencies in sample/cohort enumeration and one external-cohort accession identifier; counts and dataset provenance should therefore be preserved explicitly rather than silently reconciled.

documents.title: Uncovering the Genetic Links of SARS-CoV-2 Infections on Heart Failure Co-Morbidity by a Systems Biology Approach
documents.text:
A cross-disease transcriptomic systems-biology analysis of independently profiled COVID-19 and heart-failure datasets, identifying 12 shared genes and prioritizing inflammatory network hubs for further study.
This cross-disease multi-dataset transcriptomic systems-biology study compared independently profiled COVID-19 and heart-failure (HF) datasets. At |log2FC| > 1 and adjusted P < 0.05, the authors reported 102 COVID-19 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), 253 HF DEGs, and 12 shared genes. Enrichment analyses highlighted inflammatory and innate-immune processes, including neutrophil and monocyte chemotaxis, Toll-like receptor, NF-κB, chemokine, interleukin-17, and cytokine-related signaling. Protein-interaction topology prioritized ten hub genes, with TLR4, TLR2, IL10, and STAT3 recurring across seven cytoHubba algorithms. External public PBMC expression datasets supported prioritization of TLR4, TLR2, STAT3, IL1B, and CXCL8; the reported 96.0%, 93.2%, and 89.9% are first-two-component PCA explained-variance values, not diagnostic performance. Database-derived TF/miRNA networks highlighted FOXC1, STAT3, NFKB1, miR-181, miR-520, and miR-143, while DSigDB drug-signature enrichment nominated muramyl dipeptide and glutathione as hypothesis-generating candidates. The study did not enroll a dedicated cohort with simultaneous COVID-19 and HF, establish germline genetic correlation or causality, prospectively validate a clinical signature, experimentally validate the predicted regulatory edges, directly measure gut microbiome or circulating LPS, perform proteomics, or demonstrate treatment efficacy for the candidate compounds.

documents.title: Uncovering the Genetic Links of SARS-CoV-2 Infections on Heart Failure Co-Morbidity by a Systems Biology Approach
documents.text:
Which datasets identified the shared COVID-19 and HF genes?
The comparison used independent COVID-19 and HF transcriptomic datasets, principally GSE147507 for the human COVID-19 lung component and GSE26887 for HF left-ventricular tissue. These were separate disease datasets, not samples from a simultaneous-comorbidity cohort.

documents.title: Uncovering the Genetic Links of SARS-CoV-2 Infections on Heart Failure Co-Morbidity by a Systems Biology Approach
documents.text:
What were the 12 shared COVID-19 and HF genes?
S100A8, ABCB1, S100A11, PTGS2 (called COX2 in the article), LY96, XCL1, RORA, CCL11, CCL4, S100A12, BCL2 and AQP9 were shared at |log2FC| > 1 and adjusted P < 0.05 across the separate expression analyses.

documents.title: Uncovering the Genetic Links of SARS-CoV-2 Infections on Heart Failure Co-Morbidity by a Systems Biology Approach
documents.text:
Which genes were prioritized as network hubs?
The PPI analysis prioritized TLR4, TLR2, CXCL8, IL10, STAT3, IL1B, TLR1, TP53, CCL20 and CXCL10; seven cytoHubba algorithms converged on TLR4, TLR2, IL10 and STAT3. Network centrality is not proof of causal disease drivers.

documents.title: Uncovering the Genetic Links of SARS-CoV-2 Infections on Heart Failure Co-Morbidity by a Systems Biology Approach
documents.text:
Did the study analyze patients with both COVID-19 and HF, and what does ‘genetic links’ mean?
No dedicated cohort simultaneously affected by COVID-19 and HF was analyzed. In this paper, ‘genetic links’ refers to shared transcriptomic, gene-expression, molecular and predicted regulatory signatures across independent datasets, not germline genetic correlation, GWAS, Mendelian randomization or genetic causality.

documents.title: Uncovering the Genetic Links of SARS-CoV-2 Infections on Heart Failure Co-Morbidity by a Systems Biology Approach
documents.text:
Was the five-gene signature clinically validated, and do 96.0% and 93.2% mean diagnostic accuracy?
No prospective clinical validation or diagnostic-accuracy study was reported. The 96.0% COVID-19 and 93.2% HF values, alongside 89.9% for merged data, are variance explained by the first two PCA components in the five-gene analysis; they are not AUC, accuracy, sensitivity or specificity.

documents.title: Uncovering the Genetic Links of SARS-CoV-2 Infections on Heart Failure Co-Morbidity by a Systems Biology Approach
documents.text:
Did the study prove a gut-microbiome or circulating-LPS mechanism?
No. Gut-heart and LPS discussion is hypothesis-generating; stool microbiome composition, intestinal permeability and circulating LPS were not directly measured in this analysis.

documents.title: Uncovering the Genetic Links of SARS-CoV-2 Infections on Heart Failure Co-Morbidity by a Systems Biology Approach
documents.text:
Did glutathione or muramyl dipeptide treat COVID-19 or heart failure in this study?
No treatment efficacy was tested or demonstrated. Glutathione and muramyl dipeptide were DSigDB-prioritized in-silico drug-signature candidates based on five genes, requiring experimental and clinical evaluation before any therapeutic claim.

documents.title: Uncovering the Genetic Links of SARS-CoV-2 Infections on Heart Failure Co-Morbidity by a Systems Biology Approach
documents.text:
Why does Figure 1 mention GSE26687, and which HF dataset was used?
GSE26687 in the Figure 1 caption appears to be an accession typo. The Methods and Results, together with the formal GEO identity, identify GSE26887 as the HF cardiac-tissue dataset; the apparent typo is recorded for provenance and is not treated as a second dataset.

documents.title: Uncovering the Genetic Links of SARS-CoV-2 Infections on Heart Failure Co-Morbidity by a Systems Biology Approach
documents.text:
Which transcriptomic signatures were shared between independently profiled COVID-19 and heart-failure datasets?
Separate COVID-19 and HF expression datasets yielded a shared 12-gene transcriptomic signature; there was no dedicated cohort with both conditions.

documents.title: Uncovering the Genetic Links of SARS-CoV-2 Infections on Heart Failure Co-Morbidity by a Systems Biology Approach
documents.text:
Which inflammatory pathways were enriched across the shared COVID-HF expression signals?
Enrichment highlighted inflammatory and innate-immune pathways in shared expression signals, without establishing a causal COVID-HF mechanism.

documents.title: Uncovering the Genetic Links of SARS-CoV-2 Infections on Heart Failure Co-Morbidity by a Systems Biology Approach
documents.text:
Which network hub genes were prioritized and externally evaluated?
PPI topology nominated inflammatory hubs and external PBMC expression datasets evaluated selected genes; PCA explained variance is not classification performance.

documents.title: Uncovering the Genetic Links of SARS-CoV-2 Infections on Heart Failure Co-Morbidity by a Systems Biology Approach
documents.text:
Which predicted transcription-factor and miRNA regulatory networks were prioritized?
Database-derived TF and miRNA networks nominated computational regulatory candidates, not experimentally confirmed edges.

documents.title: Uncovering the Genetic Links of SARS-CoV-2 Infections on Heart Failure Co-Morbidity by a Systems Biology Approach
documents.text:
Which compounds were nominated by drug-signature enrichment?
Drug-signature enrichment nominated muramyl dipeptide and glutathione as hypotheses; no therapeutic efficacy was demonstrated.
